title: Accelerate your AI journey with Azure AI model catalog: Sharmila Chokalingam

summary: The session features Sharmila Chokalingam, a product marketing manager on Azure AI, and a co-presenter (product manager). They introduce the Azure AI model catalog as a platform for discovering and operationalizing foundation models across a three-stage workflow: prototyping (trying multiple models, comparing benchmarks), optimization (prompt engineering, RAG, fine-tuning), and operationalization (deployment with monitoring, scalability, data privacy, content filtering). The catalog offers over 1,600 models including flagship LLMs (GPT-4, Mistral, Llama, Cohere) and SLMs (Phi3), plus hundreds of open-source models from Hugging Face. Live demos show navigating ai.azure.com, filtering the catalog, deploying Cohere Command R via Azure Marketplace, checking model benchmarks, using the chat playground with RAG via custom data indexes, and function calling with Mistral Large for a shop chatbot with pricing and discounts. A prompt flow demo shows building a RAG-based shopping assistant with query rephrasing for improved retrieval, creating model variants to compare Cohere Command R, Llama 3, and Mistral Large, and running evaluations. Data privacy is emphasized: prompts and completions are never shared with model providers or used for training. Additional security features include model scanning for embedded malware and backdoors, private networking via VNet ingress/egress control, FQDN rules, and Azure policy integration for allow/deny lists. Two deployment options are explained: managed compute (user provisions GPUs, pays per VM hour) and serverless API (30+ flagship models, pay-per-token). Standardized APIs enable model swapping without code changes, compatible with LangChain and LiteLLM. Customer success stories include EY (EYQ chatbot adopted by 275,000 employees using OpenAI and Llama models), CMA CGM (Mistral-based customer care chatbot reducing response latency), and Bridgestone (Nixtla time series forecasting model reducing forecast errors by nearly 30%).
whyItMatters: The talk connects its engineering abstractions, implementation choices, and AI/product implications into one practical system view.

sections.title: Introduction & Session Overview
sections.summary: Presenters Sharmila (product marketing manager) and co-presenter (product manager) introduce themselves and outline the session covering model choice, standardized inference APIs, generative AI app building, enterprise requirements, and customer success stories.

sections.title: Why Model Choice Matters
sections.summary: Explains the three-stage generative AI workflow—prototyping (trying multiple models, comparing benchmarks), optimization (prompt engineering, RAG, fine-tuning), and operationalization (monitoring, scalability, data privacy, content filtering)—and how Azure AI supports each stage.

sections.title: Model Selections on Azure
sections.summary: Details the range of models offered including GPT-4, Mistral, Llama, Cohere, Phi3, Jais for Arabic, and hundreds of open-source models from Hugging Face, with partnerships with Meta, Databricks, Snowflake, and Nvidia for rapid model availability.

sections.title: Demo: Catalog Navigation & Deployment
sections.summary: Live demo navigating to ai.azure.com, filtering models by collection, viewing Cohere Command R model card with inference samples, deploying via Azure Marketplace billing, and obtaining endpoint URL and key within seconds.

sections.title: Demo: Benchmarks & Playground with RAG
sections.summary: Demonstrates model benchmarks for comparing accuracy, coherence, and groundedness, and the chat playground showing RAG by adding a custom data index (Microsoft Give) for more targeted responses with proprietary information.

sections.title: Data Privacy Assurance
sections.summary: Clarifies that customer prompts and completions are never shared with model providers and customer data is not used for training any models, addressing a common customer concern.

sections.title: Deployment Options & Standardized APIs
sections.summary: Explains two deployment options—managed compute (user-managed GPUs, pay per VM hour) and serverless API (30+ flagship models, pay-per-token)—and how standardized APIs and SDKs enable model swapping without code changes.

sections.title: Function Calling Demo
sections.summary: Live demo of function calling with Mistral Large for a shop chatbot scenario, showing how to define an external function for bill amount calculation with specific pricing and discounts, and how the model intelligently identifies function calls with correct arguments.

sections.title: Demo: Prompt Flow & Model Evaluation
sections.summary: Live demo building a RAG shopping assistant in prompt flow with query rephrasing for improved retrieval, creating model variants to compare Cohere Command R vs Llama 3 vs Mistral Large, and running evaluations to compare performance across models.

sections.title: Security, Privacy & Compliance Features
sections.summary: Details three pillars of trust: data privacy (prompts/completions not shared or used for training), security and compliance (private networking via VNet, FQDN rules, Azure policy integration for allow/deny lists), and model scanning for embedded malware, backdoors, vulnerabilities, and tampering detection.

sections.title: Customer Success Stories
sections.summary: Presents three customer stories: EY (EYQ chatbot adopted by 275K employees using OpenAI and Llama models for productivity), CMA CGM (Mistral-based customer care chatbot reducing response latency with plans to expand to invoicing and document analysis), and Bridgestone (Nixtla time series forecasting model reducing forecast errors by ~30%). Emphasizes that customers use multiple models and that Azure AI Studio reduces time from prototyping to production.
